message.content:
**Gini coefficient for the United States (most recent estimate)**  

| Year | Gini coefficient (income, household) | Source |
|------|---------------------------------------|--------|
| 2022 | **≈ 41.4** | World Bank (World Development Indicators) |
| 2021 | **≈ 41.5** | OECD (Income Distribution Database) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 100 (perfect inequality). A value of ~41 indicates a moderate level of income inequality relative to other OECD countries. The U.S. Gini is slightly lower than the OECD average (~40.8) but higher than many European nations.

> **Notes**  
> * The figures are based on pre‑tax, pre‑transfer household income.  
> * The World Bank’s 2022 estimate is the most recent publicly available figure; the OECD’s 2021 figure is the latest from that database.  
> * Both sources note that Gini estimates are subject to revisions as new data become available.
